title: LogikBench ai.json
description: AI-authorship provenance record for a single LogikBench benchmark. One ai.json sits in each AI-authored benchmark directory. It records ONLY what no other artifact captures: which model produced the RTL, the human review/sign-off, and the provenance type. The specification (function, interface, design decisions, references) lives in the benchmark README linked by spec_ref, and the file list / build recipe lives in the benchmark's Design (.py) -- those are the single sources of truth and are intentionally not duplicated here.

schema_version.description: Version of this ai.json schema the file targets.

name.description: Benchmark name (matches the block directory and Design name).

spec_ref.description: Relative path (from the benchmark directory) to the README that serves as the benchmark specification/plan. The spec is NOT duplicated here -- this is the link to it.

authorship.description: Human/organization credited with the RTL (e.g. 'Zero ASIC Corporation; author Andreas Olofsson').

generated_by.description: How the RTL was produced -- the model and interface used. This is the primary reason the file exists.

model.description: Model name/ID that authored or generated the RTL (e.g. 'claude-opus-4-8').

interface.description: Tool/interface used to drive the model (e.g. 'Claude Code').

human_review.description: Human review/sign-off on the generated RTL.

reviewed.description: Whether a human reviewed the RTL.

notes.description: Review notes / scope of the review.

type.description: original = written for LogikBench; vendored = imported as-is; derived = adapted from another source.

notes.description: Provenance notes (e.g. 'follows the cited architectures but not copied').
Optional free-form notes specific to the generation that do NOT belong in the README spec (e.g. 'regenerated after the part-select signedness fix').
